retrievalMethod: Web review tool; direct ingestion-client requests returned HTTP 403
scope: Source-authored ingredient guidance, not clinical suitability or exact-product certification. Flags measure documentation availability only.

records.title: Iron — NIH ODS Consumer Fact Sheet
records.evidenceSummary: Explains iron deficiency, anemia and life-stage requirements; more iron does not generally resolve anemia of chronic disease. Pregnancy supplementation is conditional on healthcare guidance.
records.safetySummary: Documents excessive-intake gastrointestinal effects, serious overdose toxicity and child poisoning. Hemochromatosis is a stated reason to avoid iron supplements. Documents interactions with levodopa, levothyroxine, proton-pump inhibitors and calcium. Intake and upper-limit tables vary by age and life stage.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Iron
records.referenceScope: Iron status and athletic performance, not routine supplementation of iron-replete people
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews deficiency-related work capacity and conflicting findings for iron deficiency without anemia. Cites systematic reviews and meta-analyses, while noting small studies and risk of bias. Routine supplementation is not recommended except on healthcare-provider advice.
records.safetySummary: Documents upper-intake limits, gastrointestinal adverse effects, hereditary hemochromatosis and levodopa/levothyroxine interactions. Athlete-intake context is not an individual dose recommendation.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Creatine
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews creatine for repeated high-intensity efforts and training adaptations, with variable individual responses and little value for endurance activities. Monohydrate is the most studied form; other forms are not demonstrated to be superior.
records.safetySummary: Documents water-retention weight gain, gastrointestinal complaints, cramps and hydration context, and study protocols involving loading and maintenance intakes. Guidance refers to studied populations, not a universal recommendation.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Caffeine
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews endurance and intermittent-activity studies with variable responses, timing and habituation. More caffeine is not necessarily more beneficial.
records.safetySummary: Documents sleep disturbance, anxiety, nausea and cardiovascular symptoms, adolescent cautions, stimulant-combination concerns and potentially fatal concentrated-powder overdose. Cimetidine can slow caffeine clearance. Reported intake amounts are context-specific guidance, not individual suitability advice.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Beta-alanine
records.evidenceSummary: Describes inconsistent performance findings, small heterogeneous studies and disagreement between expert reviews; performance context and study duration matter.
records.safetySummary: Documents paresthesia and itching, divided-dose or sustained-release context, and lack of long-term safety data. Includes study-dose and duration information.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Citrulline
records.referenceScope: Citrulline and citrulline malate; preparations are not interchangeable
records.evidenceSummary: Describes limited conflicting trials and distinguishes citrulline from citrulline malate and differing ingredient proportions.
records.safetySummary: Documents stomach discomfort and limited short-term intake studies; safety over months remains inadequately assessed.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Beetroot or beet juice
records.referenceScope: Beetroot juice-derived nitrate; powder products may not match studied preparations
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews variable endurance findings and differences between recreational and elite athletes. Nitrate content depends on preparation; powder supplements were not established as equivalent to studied juices.
records.safetySummary: Documents short-duration juice studies, nitrate amounts and beeturia. Longer-term supplementation data are lacking.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Sodium bicarbonate
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews conflicting high-intensity performance findings and variable individual responses; some users can experience worse performance.
records.safetySummary: Documents nausea, pain, diarrhea and vomiting, substantial sodium exposure and fluid/weight effects. Long-term ergogenic-use safety is not established.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Ginseng
records.referenceScope: Panax and so-called Siberian ginseng are distinct botanicals
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews mostly non-supportive exercise-performance studies and variation between botanical types and preparations.
records.safetySummary: Documents headaches, sleep and gastrointestinal effects, short-term study scope and warfarin interaction information.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Protein
records.referenceScope: General protein guidance including whey; not a product-specific protein review
records.evidenceSummary: Reviews total protein intake, training response, recovery, timing and essential amino-acid composition; protein sources differ.
records.safetySummary: Provides athlete-intake guidance and discusses studied high-protein diets, with caution about limited adverse-effect data and no established upper limit.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Protein and casein
records.referenceScope: General protein guidance and casein studies
records.evidenceSummary: Describes slower casein digestion, pre-sleep studies and the importance of total protein intake and amino-acid supply.
records.safetySummary: General protein safety and intake guidance; not a casein-specific purity or allergen certification.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Protein sources
records.referenceScope: General protein guidance including soy, rice and complementary plant sources
records.evidenceSummary: Discusses protein-source amino-acid differences and complementary sources; a blend's formulation must be identified independently.
records.safetySummary: General athlete protein intake and studied high-protein diet context; not verification of an individual plant-protein product.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Antioxidants
records.referenceScope: Antioxidant guidance in exercise, not general deficiency treatment
records.evidenceSummary: Discusses trials in which large antioxidant intakes did not directly improve performance and might blunt some training adaptations.
records.safetySummary: Documents gastrointestinal effects of excess vitamin C, upper-intake context and potential interference of high-dose antioxidants with chemotherapy/radiotherapy.

records.title: NIH ODS Exercise and Athletic Performance — Coenzyme Q10
records.evidenceSummary: Reports limited ergogenic support and a small trial suggesting poorer adaptation to training; this does not establish ineffectiveness for other contexts.
records.safetySummary: Lists gastrointestinal, sleep, skin and other possible side effects and short-duration study context.
